title: Credibility assessment of explicit-dynamics head protection models under ASME V&V40 for skull and brain kinematics
runhead: V&V40 assessment of cranial protection models
device: Cranial impact protection system intended to attenuate skull and brain kinematics during head impacts

models.name: Helmeted Rigid-Skull Kinematics (HRK) model
models.what_it_computes: Explicit FEA of helmet–head assembly with a rigid skull surrogate to predict skull center-of-gravity linear and angular accelerations, impact force time histories, and contact metrics

models.name: Skull–Brain Dynamics (SBD) model
models.what_it_computes: Explicit FEA with anatomically detailed skull, meninges, CSF layer, and brain to predict skull kinematics, brain bulk motion (angular velocity/acceleration), and tissue-level maximum principal strain

mechanisms.name: Normal drop impact
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Represents vertical energy transfer typical of falls and some sports collisions; primarily challenges linear acceleration attenuation and peak force management

mechanisms.name: Oblique impact with tangential loading
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Introduces coupled normal–tangential loading and head rotation relevant to diffuse brain injury risk; challenges rotational kinematics mitigation by liners and slip interfaces

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–8 Credibility Evidence Scale (CES), where 0 denotes no evidence and 8 denotes convergent, multi-source evidence; half-point scores are permitted

sections: Introduction
